conclusions: Observed D installation launch, Traditional Chinese guide and uninstall shortcuts remain in the distinct Mir2 联网试玩版 group and target D:/Mir2Invite. No actual path collision with the first validation group was observed.
Without a preinstall .lnk snapshot, historical shortcut byte preservation cannot be certified. Existing registry/game/preference snapshots do not prove shortcut preservation.
The first log explicitly created the new Numeron group, and all three observed new links targeted only the validation installation.

commandLinePolicy.explanation: /GROUP is ignored when DisableProgramGroupPage=yes. /NOICONS initializes the optional no-group checkbox; AllowNoIcons defaults to no. The three unconditional group entries have no Tasks parameter.

minimalRecoverySuggestion: Do not recreate or repoint legacy D shortcuts without evidence of damage; no such repair is currently indicated.

Before another installation, archive the current exact validation links and snapshot the old group hashes. If cleaning first-attempt shortcuts, remove only the three exact known test links after confirming both target and recorded hash; remove their parent only if empty. Do not recursively delete the group or touch legacy links. No cleanup was executed by this audit.

A standalone /GROUP unique argument is insufficient with the current hidden group page. Without recipe changes, use and snapshot the known separate validation group and remove exact test entries afterward.

If the coordinator already rebuilds the installer for the independent updater fix, a validation-only unique DefaultGroupName plus UsePreviousGroup=no gives a stable isolated group; alternatively validation-only DisableProgramGroupPage=no makes an explicit /GROUP override effective. Keep normal installer behavior unchanged.
publicClaimsToAvoid: All old shortcuts remained byte-identical after first installation.
/NOICONS or /TASKS="" suppressed every Start Menu shortcut.
/GROUP alone isolates this current compiled installer.
